forecaster_note: Breezy offshores. Small clean surf picks up later in the day as new south swell comes in. Small peaky surf in the morning from leftover ENE swell mix — about waist to occasionally chest high. Picking up later afternoon at the south magnets as some new south swell builds through the day; probably going head high or so there, but staying relatively small elsewhere. Clean with breezy offshore winds. — Hugh McDowell, Surfline Sydney

wind.summary: Breezy WSW offshore, 15–16kph with 25–39kph gusts at dawn, easing to 11–12kph W by midday. Clean all day.

shark.summary: No SMART drumline alerts or tagged-shark detections anywhere on the NSW coast in the last 48 hours. SharkSmart feed confirmed live (SLSNSW drone layer updated 4:56am today).

days.label: Today
days.note: Breezy W–WSW offshore all day and it only gets lighter — cleanest window is 9am–1pm. Morning is leftover ENE peaks on a short-period SSW mix, then a new south swell fills in through the afternoon, so the south-facing corners will be the ones that grow. Low tide 12:37pm keeps the banks working mid-morning.

dee-why.window: 9:30am–12:30pm. Tide draining to the 12:37pm low keeps the bank punchy — Point corner best on the ENE lines before the S fills in.

tip.label: Frontside at the Point
tip.text: Only 188 kJ at mid-morning and the SSW is a 7s windswell — it'll be short and fast, not powerful. Sit on the ENE 9s lines off the Point for your rights and stay high through the first turn; the S component wraps in weak here so don't wait for it.

long-reef.window: 9am–12pm. Biggest of the four this morning — it's grabbing the SSW that Dee Why misses.

tip.label: Frontside, the size magnet
tip.text: Long Reef is doubling Dee Why on the same 188 kJ because the 214° SSW swings straight in. Expect chest-to-head sets with gaps between — 7s period means they stack up fast and close out if you sit too deep. Take the ones with the ENE 9s underneath them.

curl-curl.window: 9am–12pm on the draining tide. Best all-round blend of size and shape today.

tip.label: Pick your bank
tip.text: Curl Curl sits between Dee Why's shelter and Long Reef's exposure — waist-to-shoulder with a clean 15kph WSW brushing it. Walk the beach before you paddle out: at 188 kJ the wave quality is all bank, not swell.

manly.window: 9am–12pm, but it's the smallest option. Worth it only if you want an easy paddle.

tip.label: Backside on the lefts
tip.text: North Steyne is the most sheltered of the four from a 214° swell — thigh-to-stomach and soft. If you go, the S pulse arriving late arvo will actually help here more than this morning does.

days.label: Tomorrow
days.note: Best day of the next three. 100% consistency, a genuine 4.7ft @ 10s south swell in the water plus 2.4ft @ 9s ENE, and offshore NW→W wind all day. It peaks in the morning and slowly eases, so go early-to-mid morning — 8am–11am.

dee-why.window: 8am–11am while it's peaking. Eases through the afternoon.

long-reef.window: 8am–11am. Pick of the coast tomorrow — fair-to-good rating with a 10s S swell and light NW–W.

curl-curl.window: 8am–11am. Clean and rippable before the swell drops off.

manly.window: 8am–10am. Smallest again — only if you want a mellow one.

days.label: Weekend
days.note: Long-period south swell takes over — 318 kJ Saturday, the biggest energy of the week. But the direction is the problem: 173° Sat and 154° Sun, near dead south, and S/SE onshores arrive from mid-morning both days. Dawn to 9am is the only clean window. Saturday is the better of the two.

dee-why.window: Sat dawn–9am only. 173° is almost dead south — it wraps in weak and gutless at Dee Why despite the 318 kJ. Sunday worse (154°, onshore from first light).
alerts: S/SE onshore from mid-morning both days
Dead-south direction — energy doesn't translate here

long-reef.window: Sat 6:30–9am. Takes the south swell better than anywhere else on this stretch — head-high-plus before the wind ruins it.
alerts: Cross-shore S from 9am Saturday, onshore all Sunday

curl-curl.window: Sat dawn–9am. Size is there but expect closeouts on a 7s short-period south.

manly.window: Sat early. Most sheltered — smallest but likely holds shape longest as the S/SE fills in.
alerts: S/SE onshore both days from mid-morning
